checks: Verified original §3 for the corrected supporting face, coverage and unnormalized nested continuation. The original does not spell out the full-own reduction; the normalized proof supplies it explicitly from compatible anchored capture.

A selected cap through a buffered interior source cannot have zero own mass. In the proper case all larger thresholds strictly reduce its own cap mass, so its old mass-Q threshold is the right Q endpoint. Every other deepest mark has cap mass at least Q in this direction, giving the desired inequality.

In the full-own case, choosing strictly missed points excludes p from the convex hull of the not-wholly-captured bases by compatibility. Strict separation through p gives a trace T consisting only of full fibers. Atomic depth at p is at least Q and the ambient cap has mass Q, so T has mass Q, all remaining fibers have zero cap volume, and no full positive-volume fiber lies outside T.

If q≠p belongs to T, shifting a strict interior q to the boundary retains strict exclusion of P\T while excluding p. If q lies on the separator, adding η(q−p) through q excludes p and preserves those finitely many strict exclusions for small positive η. This also handles the whole base with a=0; no distinct q arises in rank zero. The new base trace has mass at most Q−|K_p|, contrary to q deepest. At every remaining deepest base a strictly positive ambient margin anywhere would give positive volume, so the needed threshold comparison holds everywhere there.

With the continuous balance, the weighted shifted margin is the corrected base functional plus ε times a nonnegative supergradient gap. The functional is nonpositive on the deepest hull and zero on the minimal face, including the case of a zero resultant. Over that face weighted old margins dominate the buffer; the smaller buffer and nested measure keep one old mass-Q threshold an upper bound at every mark.
